answer: Duplication-Linked Deposit Forfeiture. Each identity posts a distinct umber-coded deposit at registration. To act, it must periodically submit a fresh, single-use root derived from that deposit. Cloned identities necessarily reuse roots, and the reef ledger flags the collision, freezing both deposits. An attacker duplicating one agent pays a full forfeited deposit per clone, since every copy triggers a harbor-wide lockout that seizes the original too. Cost scales linearly with clone count, making duplication self-revealing.
